observations: Rule 6a tests the presence of `needs.<X>.result`, not what it is compared with: `always() && needs.x.result != 'failure' && needs.x.outputs.skip != 'true'` passes the checker (probe p13, exit 0) and GitHub runs it on a SKIPPED x — the probe run's hazard_ne_failure job ran to success with `result=skipped`. That is the plan's rule as written (`tests needs.<X>.result`) and the spec's letter; every result test in the three workflows today is `== 'success'` or `== 'skipped'`. Whether 6a should require `== 'success'` (or refuse `!=`) is a rule change for the architect, not a defect in this implementation; no red test written.

The index form rule 6 reads is the job's (`needs['x'].outputs`), as the header says; `needs.x['outputs'].skip` (GitHub's property-dereference index on the property itself) is not read as an outputs read, so `always() && needs.legion_build['outputs'].skip != 'true'` passes (probe p3, exit 0). Legal but unidiomatic GitHub syntax that nothing in the repository writes; recorded as a limit of the tripwire's named patterns, not a failure.

The implementer's filesChanged and proof say `fourteen red cases`; the harness has 13 red cases (30 checks) plus the index form's green half, the casing green case and the step-level green case. Wording only; the counts of checks (221; 191/30 against main's checker) are right.

The literal strip `'(?:[^']|'')*'` is correct for an empty literal followed by another literal (I expected `''` to be read as an escaped quote and swallow the text between; the leading `'` of the pattern consumes the first quote, so `''` closes). Verified in Python on four shapes and by probes p1/p12.
